
# Advanced Customisation

## Priority Icons

One of the most useful things we can do now we've switched to the three-step animation is to apply custom icons to patients with different priorities.

This allows us to better see how they behave in our models.


## A note - VidigiStore vs VidigiPriorityStore

Just like `simpy.Resource` and `simpy.PriorityResource`, we have their analogues `VidigiStore` and `VidigiPriorityStore`.

So for an animation that uses priority, we'd have

::: {.codewindow .python}
g_three_step_animation_custom_priority_icons.py
```{.python}
from vidigi.resources import VidigiPriorityStore
```
:::

And, imagining we have a single priority resource, we'd set it up like this:

::: {.codewindow .python}
g_three_step_animation_custom_priority_icons.py
```{.python}
class Model:
    def __init__(self, param, replication_id):
        ...
        self.nurse = VidigiPriorityStore(
            self.env,
            num_resources=self.param.num_nurses,
            label="nurse",
            logger=self.logger,
        )
```
:::

## Requesting a resource with priority

We pass the priority in exactly as we would for a Simpy PriorityResource - alongside the arguments we already met for `VidigiStore`.

```{.python code-line-style="dim:1,focus:2,dim:3-6" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
with self.nurse.request(
    priority=patient.priority,  # NEW
    entity_id=patient.id,
    start_event="being_seen_by_nurse",
    end_event="nurse_treatment_ends",
) as req:
    ...
```

## Recording priority in our event logs

::: {style='font-size: 75%;'}
Every vidigi logging step can record any number of additional things about an entity, so we can add an entity's priority.

We'll call our extra field `patient_priority` - it's separate from the `priority` argument that controls the queue.
:::

::: {.codewindow .python}
g_three_step_animation_custom_priority_icons.py
```{.python code-line-style="dim:1-4,focus:5,dim:6-12,focus:13,dim:14-20,focus:21,dim:22-32,focus:33,dim:34" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
def attend_clinic(self, patient):
    patient.arrival_time = self.env.now
    self.logger.log_arrival(
        entity_id=patient.id,
        patient_priority=patient.priority,
    )

    start_q_nurse = self.env.now

    self.logger.log_queue(
        entity_id=patient.id,
        event="nurse_wait_begins",
        patient_priority=patient.priority,
    )

    with self.nurse.request(
        priority=patient.priority,
        entity_id=patient.id,
        start_event="being_seen_by_nurse",
        end_event="nurse_treatment_ends",
        patient_priority=patient.priority,
    ) as req:
        yield req

        end_q_nurse = self.env.now
        patient.q_time_nurse = end_q_nurse - start_q_nurse

        sampled_nurse_act_time = self.nurse_consult_time_dist.sample()
        yield self.env.timeout(sampled_nurse_act_time)

    self.logger.log_departure(
        entity_id=patient.id,
        patient_priority=patient.priority,
    )
```
:::


## EventLog with priority recorded

Let's now take a quick look at our event log. We can see that it now has a priority column!

```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| label: priority-model-display-event-log

import itables
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML
itables.init_notebook_mode(all_interactive=True)
itables.options.lengthMenu = [10]
itables.options.layout["topStart"] = None
display(HTML("<style>.dt-container { font-size: 20pt; }</style>"))

from sample_code.g_three_step_animation_custom_priority_icons import Param, Model

import os
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(os.environ["QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR"])

patient_iat_csv = PROJECT_ROOT / "sample_code" / "nspp_example_dataset.csv"

my_params = Param(num_nurses=2,
    patient_iat_csv=patient_iat_csv,
    num_nurses_unav=0,  # Switch off nurse obstruction for this example
    warm_up_period=0
    )
my_model = Model(my_params, replication_id=1)
my_model.run_model()

my_event_log = my_model.logger.to_dataframe()

my_event_log
```


## Animating

Now, if we just run the three step animation as-is, we won't see any impact of the priority resource unless we watch very closely...

```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| label: non-priority-icon-demo-animation

from vidigi.prep import reshape_for_animations, generate_animation_df
from vidigi.animation import generate_animation
from vidigi.utils import create_event_position_df, EventPosition

# The layout in sample_code/g_three_step_animation_custom_priority_icons.py is defined
# inside the `if __name__ == "__main__"` block, so it can't be imported.
# Keep this copy in sync with that file.
layout = create_event_position_df(
    [
        EventPosition(event="arrival", x=0, y=350, label="Entrance"),
        EventPosition(
            event="nurse_wait_begins", x=200, y=250, label="Waiting for Nurse"
        ),
        EventPosition(
            event="being_seen_by_nurse",
            x=200,
            y=150,
            label="Being Seen By Nurse",
            resource="num_nurses",
        ),
        EventPosition(event="depart", x=200, y=50, label="Exit"),
    ]
)

reshaped_df = reshape_for_animations(
    event_log=my_event_log,
    every_x_time_units=1,
    limit_duration=my_params.sim_duration,
)

animation_df = generate_animation_df(
    full_entity_df=reshaped_df,
    event_position_df=layout,
)

fig = generate_animation(
    full_entity_df_plus_pos=animation_df,
    event_position_df=layout,
    scenario=my_params,
    plotly_height=500,
    plotly_width=1000
)


HTML(fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs="cdn", auto_play=False))
```


## Creating a custom function for assigning icons

We are going to create a new function. It looks at each row of our animation dataframe and decides which icon that entity should have.

::: {.codewindow .python}
g_three_step_animation_custom_priority_icons.py
```{.python}
def show_priority_icon(row):
    # First check this isn't a '+ y more' row
    if "more" not in row["icon"]:
        if row["patient_priority"] == 1:
            return "🚨"
        if row["patient_priority"] == 2:
            return "⚠️"
        else:
            return row["icon"]
    else:
        return row["icon"]
```
:::

## Applying our custom function

We apply this function to every row using a combination of `assign` and `apply`.

It needs to be applied **after** we run `generate_animation_df()`, as that's the point at which the standard icons have been assigned to each entity, so we can intervene and overwrite them.

::: {.codewindow .python style="width:100%;"}
g_three_step_animation_custom_priority_icons.py
```{.python code-line-style="dim:1-4,focus:5-7,dim:8-9" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
reshaped_df = reshape_for_animations(...)

animation_df = generate_animation_df(...)

animation_df = animation_df.assign(
    icon=animation_df.apply(show_priority_icon, axis=1)
)

fig = generate_animation(...)
```
:::

## Taking a look at the animation df

After we've applied our custom function, let's take a look at our icon column...

```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| label: priority-icon-demo-animation-df

from vidigi.prep import reshape_for_animations, generate_animation_df
from vidigi.animation import generate_animation

reshaped_df = reshape_for_animations(
    event_log=my_event_log,
    every_x_time_units=1,
    limit_duration=my_params.sim_duration,
)

animation_df = generate_animation_df(
    full_entity_df=reshaped_df,
    event_position_df=layout,
)

def show_priority_icon(row):
    # First check this isn't a '+ y more' row
    if "more" not in row["icon"]:
        if row["patient_priority"] == 1:
            return "🚨"
        if row["patient_priority"] == 2:
            return "⚠️"
        else:
            return row["icon"]
    else:
        return row["icon"]

animation_df = animation_df.assign(
            icon=animation_df.apply(show_priority_icon, axis=1)
        )

animation_df[["entity_id", "event_type", "event", "time", "resource_id", "patient_priority", "snapshot_time", "icon"]].head(200)
```

[**\* some columns hidden**]{style="color:yellow; font-size:75%"}

## BONUS: Adding extra information to icons

::: {style='font-size: 75%;'}
Because patient icons are just text, we can add other useful information in!

A useful one might be the wait time.

First, we make a new column that compares the `snapshot_time` (the time it is in the animation) with the `time` (the time the current event started).
:::

```{.python code-line-style="dim:1-2,focus:3" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
reshaped_df = reshape_for_animations(...)
animation_df = generate_animation_df(...)
animation_df["time_in_step"] = animation_df["snapshot_time"] - animation_df["time"]
```

```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| label: extra-info-demo-setup

import random
animation_df["time_in_step"] = animation_df["snapshot_time"] - animation_df["time"]
random.seed(42)
animation_df[["entity_id", "event", "time", "snapshot_time", "time_in_step", "icon"]].sample(3).sort_values("snapshot_time")
```


## BONUS: Adding extra information to icons - continued

We can then modify our existing step

```{.python}
def add_time_in_step(row):
    # First check this isn't a '+ y more' row
    if "more" not in row["icon"]:
        return row["icon"] + "<br>" + f"{row["time_in_step"]:.0f}"
    else:
        return row["icon"]
```

and then call this in the same way as before.

```{.python code-line-style="dim:1-7,focus:8-10" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
reshaped_df = reshape_for_animations(...)
animation_df = generate_animation_df(...)

animation_df = animation_df.assign(
    icon=animation_df.apply(show_priority_icon, axis=1)
)

animation_df = animation_df.assign(
    icon=animation_df.apply(add_time_in_step, axis=1)
)
```


```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| label: additional-info-demo-add-info
def add_time_in_step(row):
    # First check this isn't a '+ y more' row
    if "more" not in row["icon"]:
        return row["icon"] + "<br>" + f"{row["time_in_step"]:.0f}"
    else:
        return row["icon"]


animation_df = generate_animation_df(
    full_entity_df=reshaped_df,
    event_position_df=layout,
    gap_between_queue_rows=65,
    wrap_queues_at=15
)

animation_df["time_in_step"] = animation_df["snapshot_time"] - animation_df["time"]

animation_df = animation_df.assign(
            icon=animation_df.apply(show_priority_icon, axis=1)
        )

animation_df = animation_df.assign(
            icon=animation_df.apply(add_time_in_step, axis=1)
        )
```
